nodes.label: Asynchronous Programming
nodes.description: Patterns for non-blocking code execution where operations can start now and finish later, without halting the main thread.

nodes.label: Concurrency Models
nodes.description: High-level strategies for running multiple tasks in overlapping time periods: cooperative (event loop) vs. preemptive (threads).

nodes.label: Error Handling
nodes.description: Approaches to detecting, propagating, and recovering from runtime failures in code.

nodes.label: Modules & Packaging
nodes.description: Mechanisms for organizing code into reusable units and managing external dependencies.

nodes.label: Streams & Buffers
nodes.description: APIs for processing continuous flows of data in chunks rather than loading everything into memory at once.

nodes.label: HTTP & Networking
nodes.description: Core protocols and patterns for client–server communication over the web, including request/response and real-time channels.

nodes.label: Data Structures
nodes.description: Built-in and library types for organizing data in memory: arrays, objects (maps), sets, queues, etc.

nodes.label: JS Syntax Basics
nodes.description: Literals, statements, comments, semicolon rules and basic language grammar in JavaScript.

nodes.label: JS Control Flow
nodes.description: `if/else`, `switch`, loops (`for`, `while`, `for…of`, `for…in`) and conditional expressions in JS.

nodes.label: JS Modules & Imports
nodes.description: ES module (`import`/`export`) and CommonJS (`require`/`module.exports`) syntax and semantics.

nodes.label: JS Asynchronous Patterns
nodes.description: Callbacks, Promises, and `async/await` to handle deferred operations in JavaScript.

nodes.label: Node.js Event Loop & Worker Threads
nodes.description: How Node.js schedules callbacks on its single-threaded event loop and offloads CPU-bound work to worker threads.

nodes.label: JS Error Handling
nodes.description: `try`/`catch`/`finally`, `throw`, and best practices for propagating and recovering from exceptions in Node.js.

nodes.label: JS Streams & Buffers
nodes.description: Using Node.js `stream` APIs and `Buffer` class to process large or continuous data efficiently.

nodes.label: JS HTTP Servers & REST APIs
nodes.description: Building web servers and RESTful endpoints using `http`, Express, or Fastify.

nodes.label: JS WebSockets & Real-Time Streams
nodes.description: Implementing bi-directional real-time communication via WebSockets or libraries like Socket.IO.

nodes.label: npm/Yarn Package Management
nodes.description: Dependency installation, semantic versioning, lockfiles, and scripts in `package.json`.

nodes.label: JSON & File I/O
nodes.description: Reading and writing JSON or other config files from disk using `fs` and managing environment variables.

nodes.label: TensorFlow.js Integration
nodes.description: Loading and running pre-trained ML models (e.g. Transformers) in Node.js via TensorFlow.js or ONNX Runtime.

nodes.label: Database Connectivity
nodes.description: Using drivers/ORMs (MongoDB, PostgreSQL, Redis) to persist and query data in Node.js applications.

nodes.label: Performance Profiling & Debugging
nodes.description: CPU/memory profiling (`--inspect`, flamegraphs), logging, and best practices to find bottlenecks.

nodes.label: Deployment & Scaling
nodes.description: Containerizing (Docker), orchestration (Kubernetes), load-balancing and autoscaling Node.js services.
